q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of a tractor trailer?
title: Tractor trailer carbon footprint per trailer
short: Weigh the steel chassis, body sheet, axle and hitch per trailer and multiply by supplier figures, then add the tyres. Add cutting, welding, painting and assembly energy, then divide the workshop's energy by trailers built.

ul: Steel channels and sheet for chassis and body.
Tyres, paint and hydraulic tipping parts if fitted.

p: Report per trailer by payload and weight. Steel is usually most of the footprint, so a lighter design lowers it directly.

example.title: Worked example: plant energy per trailer (one month)
lines: Plant total: 20,160 / 150 = 134.4 kg CO2 per trailer
Add steel, axle and tyres for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
